name: Osaki
tagline: Shinagawa in 3 minutes and Shibuya in 8 minutes. Served by 4 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Shinagawa City, where JR East and Tokyo Waterfront Area Rapid Transit run 4 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 25 minutes to Otemachi, 13 minutes to Shinjuku, 8 minutes to Shibuya and 3 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 3.7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 16.9 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 3.7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.7 m to 20.6 m, a difference of 16.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 6 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 6 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. The station itself is inside the projected area, but few of the points around it are. Compared with other stations in the 23 wards, the flood projection here is on the small side.

groceries.name: まいばすけっと 大崎駅前店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 6 clinics and 9 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 有仁会阿部病院, about 14 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 河野臨牀医学研究所附属第三北品川病院, about 16 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 4 lines serve the station. JR Yamanote Line and JR Saikyo Line run through it. JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line and Rinkai Line also call here. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 3 lines and Tokyo Waterfront Area Rapid Transit runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: JR Saikyo Line runs at 167% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 板橋→池袋, which this station is not on. JR Yamanote Line runs at 136%. Its busiest stretch is 新大久保→新宿, which this station is likewise not on. Rinkai Line runs at 118% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大井町→品川シーサイド; trains from here toward 品川シーサイド pass through it. JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line is not covered by the ministry's congestion survey. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. 1LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000 and 2LDK ¥300,000 to ¥310,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the lowest in the 23 wards. In plain yen, though, it is on the high side for the 23 wards. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For how easy the shopping is, Osaki-Hirokoji; for how close the centre is, Osaki.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Osaki. Osaki adds the 4 lines; Osaki-Hirokoji adds the Tokyu Ikegami Line. Osaki is at least 9 minutes quicker to Shinjuku and Tokyo. A one-room flat also costs about ¥10,000 more at Osaki-Hirokoji. On how easy the shopping is, though, Osaki-Hirokoji comes out ahead. Within about 13 minutes' walk, Osaki-Hirokoji has 12 supermarkets (東急ストア and 成城石井 and others) and Osaki has 7.

neighbours.lead: Osaki is ahead on lower rent, and little else separates the two.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Osaki. Both have the JR Yamanote Line. Osaki adds the JR Saikyo Line, JR Shonan-Shinjuku Line and Rinkai Line; Gotanda adds the Tokyu Ikegami Line and Toei Asakusa Line. Osaki is 5 minutes quicker to Shinjuku, but times to the other main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat costs about ¥13,000 more at Gotanda.

noiseSources: 山手通り (2 lanes each way) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 7 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 4 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the lowest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Rinkai Line trains toward 品川シーサイド pass through the line's busiest stretch, but at 118% passengers are not shoulder to shoulder.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
